changes.before: Replace the two values with an empty vector. What prints?
changes.after: Use an iterator to walk through a sequence without reading past its end.

before: begin() identifies the first element; end() identifies one past the last. The notation [begin, end) includes begin but excludes end. Never dereference end.
An iterator supports operations appropriate to its category. Here ++it moves to the next vector element and *it accesses the current element. Compare to end before dereferencing.
For an empty vector, begin() equals end(), so this loop executes zero times. No special dereference is needed to discover emptiness.

Expected output or behavior: 6
. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Trace the same loop with three values, writing the iterator’s current value before each advance. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: An iterator identifies a position in a sequence. begin() marks the first item when one exists. end() marks a position just after the last item, so end itself is not an item to read.
*it reaches the item at the iterator's current position. ++it advances this iterator to the next position. The loop uses these operations to visit the vector's values.
The condition it != values.end() runs before the body. It keeps the loop from reading the past-the-end position.
The program prints 6. The loop reads two and then four, adding both to the total. It stops when the iterator reaches end().
For an empty vector, begin() already equals end(). The first test is false, so there is no item access and the total stays at its starting value.

before.question: Replace the two values with an empty vector. What prints?
choices: 0, because the range has no elements
before.explanation: begin equals end before the first iteration, and total was initialized to zero.

after.question: Replace the vector's contents with an empty vector. What prints?
choices: 0, because there are no items to add.
The program reads an invalid item.
An unknown integer because total has no starting value.
after.explanation: total starts at zero. begin() equals end(), so the loop body never runs.
